en: Last night, oh Nannina, I went up,
you know where, you know where,
where this ungrateful heart can spite me
no more! (No more)
Where the fire burns, but if you flee
it leaves you be! (It leaves you be!)
And it does not run after you, it does not wear you away
just by looking (just by looking).
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
funiculì, funiculà!
up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
Girl, let's go from the land to the mountain!
It is only a step! It is only a step!
One sees France, Procida and Spain...
I see you! I see you!
Pulled by the rope, no sooner said than done,
up to the sky one goes, up to the sky one goes.
One goes like the wind, all of a sudden,
hey, up it climbs, up [?]!
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
funiculì, funiculà!
up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
It has gone up, oh girl, it has gone up,
my head already! (My head already!)
It went, then it turned back, then it came,
it is always here! (It is always here!)
My head turns, turns, around, around,
around you! Around you!
This heart always sings the same old refrain:
Let's get married, oh girl! Let's get married, oh girl!
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
Let's go, let's go up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
funiculì, funiculà!
up, let's go, come on,
funiculì, funiculà!
notes: Funiculì, funiculà plays on funicolare, the funicular railway; the words are kept as they are.
Line 1.1: Nanninè, a pet form of Anna (Nannina); aisséra, 'yesterday evening'. Lines 3.1, 5.1 and 5.8: né, oje né, short for Nennè or Nanninè: 'girl', 'dear'.
Lines 1.3-1.4: literally 'where this ungrateful heart can do me no more spite'.
Line 1.5: the fire is the volcano's, on the mountain the funicular climbs.
Line 1.7: nun te struje, 'it does not consume (destroy) you'.
Refrain: jamme jà, 'let's go, come on'; 'ncoppa, 'up', 'to the top'.
Line 3.8: guè is 'hey'; saglie, 'it climbs' or 'climb!'; sà is uncertain, perhaps a clipped repetition of saglie.
Lines 5.1-5.2: 'it has gone up, my head', i.e. the singer's head is in a whirl; capa, 'head'.
Line 5.7: 'nt'o taluorno, 'in the taluorno': a Neapolitan word for a tiresome, endless repetition or lament.
